2608.29136.title: Not the Same Protector: Deployment-Dependent Protective Intervention in LLMs
2608.29136.paper_summary: We ask whether a model protects a user in the same way when that user speaks rather than types. Using a single distress vignette---a physical injury of unstated severity following an interpersonal conflict---we present four frontier models with matched inputs across voice, text, and raw API deployment conditions (n=30 per cell) and code each response along five binary protective indicators, including whether the model issues an explicit medical-care directive. Voice-interface responses are markedly shorter than text-interface responses for three of the four models, and protective behavior contracts alongside that compression: medical directives are at ceiling under both the API and text conditions but decline under voice for every model tested. The contraction is not reducible to length. One model produces voice and text responses of comparable length yet still drops medical directives, and another falls below ceiling between its API and voice conditions, whose responses are of nearly identical length. Under raw API access the pattern is categorical rather than partial: no model asks after the user's safety even once. These results show that protective intervention is sensitive to the surface through which a request arrives, that this sensitivity is detectable using a simple protective coding scheme, and that it is not explained by turn length alone.
2608.29136.paper_summary_zh: 我們詢問當用戶說話而不是打字時，模型是否以相同的方式保護用戶。使用一個單一的困擾情境——在一場人際衝突後發生的未明嚴重程度的身體傷害——我們展示了四個前沿模型，並在語音、文本和原始API部署條件下匹配輸入（每個單元n=30），並根據五個二元保護指標對每個回應進行編碼，包括模型是否發出明確的醫療護理指令。在四個模型中，語音介面的回應顯著比文本介面的回應短，而保護行為隨著這種壓縮而減少：在API和文本條件下，醫療指令達到上限，但在語音條件下對每個測試的模型均有所下降。這種收縮無法簡單歸因於長度。一個模型產生的語音和文本回應長度相當，但仍然未發出醫療指令，另一個模型在其API和語音條件之間的表現低於上限，這兩者的回應長度幾乎相同。在原始API訪問下，這種模式是類別性的而非部分性的：沒有模型甚至一次也未詢問用戶的安全性。這些結果顯示，保護性干預對請求到達的表面敏感，這種敏感性可以通過簡單的保護編碼方案檢測到，並且並非僅僅由回合長度解釋。
